subject: Feasibility: consolidated privacy addendum for banking + health pilot
messages:
From: Benjamin Larson <benjamin.larson@harborbank.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: legal@harborbank.com
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: consolidated privacy addendum for pilot (GLBA + BAA)

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the intro on the vendor side — I'm Benjamin on the Harbor Bank vendor intake team. We're evaluating Redwood for a small pilot that will process both customer financial data (GLBA scope) and a subset of health-related claims data (PHI). Before we go deeper technically, our legal and security teams asked whether Redwood can do a consolidated privacy addendum that covers GLBA obligations and a BAA for the PHI portion, plus a clear subprocessor and residency stance for US-only and EU-US transfers.

Attached is a short questionnaire the team filled out with the main items (HarborBank_DPA_Questions.pdf). High-level asks:
- Can you support a combined DPA + BAA or do you prefer separate addenda?
- Can Redwood guarantee no persistent logging of PHI and limit any logs to ephemeral trace spans?
- What subprocessors would be in-scope and can we get EU residency for models and logs if needed?
- Timeline: pilot kickoff target is mid-December; we need a feasibility check this week.

Who should I loop in from Redwood? Also, is there a short residency/capacity matrix you can share?

Best,
Benjamin Larson
Vendor Intake | Harbor Bank

+1 (415) 555-0198

Short answers up front: we can support both GLBA and HIPAA/BAA use cases; we typically surface a DPA with addenda for GLBA and a BAA when PHI is involved. That said, we can propose a consolidated addendum where appropriate — happy to review the HarborBank questionnaire and propose language.

I've attached a quick residency/capacity matrix (Redwood_Residency_Matrix.xlsx) to give you a sense of what we offer by region and deployment mode (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private).

Proposed next step: 30-min alignment call tomorrow to run through the questionnaire and confirm whether you need EU residency for any part of this pilot. Can your team do 10:00–10:30am PT on Tue 11/3?

Attendees from our side will be: Markus Klein (Product Infra), Monica Patel (Legal Ops), and Evelyn Hart (Customer Security).

Thanks — talk soon.

Subject: Fwd: HarborBank privacy addendum feasibility — pre-read and asks

Folks — forwarding HarborBank's questionnaire and my note back. Call is 10:00am PT today. Quick pre-read and my asks below so we can be aligned on the call:

Summary (from our side):
- Customer wants to process GLBA-covered data + a small PHI subset. They asked for a consolidated DPA + BAA if possible.
- They want explicit subprocessor list, residency options, and confirmation around logging and retention for PHI.

Asks: 
- Markus: please be prepared to speak to dedicated capacity vs. hosted routing, per-customer KV cache isolation, and KMS/HSM integration. Also note any limits on EU residency for model weights vs telemetry.
- Monica: legal review — what are our recommended contract patterns? Consolidated addendum or separate DPA + BAA? Any redlines we should flag early?
- Evelyn: security quick wins (encryption at rest, audit log retention defaults, SOC2/ISO evidence) we can reference in the call.

I'll capture any blocking items and follow up after the call with a consolidated action plan and a draft addendum if legal recommends.

Thanks — G.

--
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales, Regulated Verticals | Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: HarborBank privacy addendum feasibility — pre-read and asks

Quick technical notes following the pre-call and our alignment:

1) Residency and model artifacts
- Hosted API: model weights run on multi-tenant clusters; we can pin inference to region (us-east, us-west, eu-west) but cannot guarantee exclusive physical host tenancy without Dedicated/Private.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools provide tenancy isolation and enable keeping logs and model artifacts inside a region; recommended for GLBA+PHI pilots that need strong residency guarantees.

2) Logging and PHI
- We can configure the runtime to avoid persistent storage of request payloads for specific routes (ephemeral only, 0 retention).
- Trace spans and debug logs can be masked; we recommend a policy of no persistent PHI in logs and tokenization rules for the pilot.

3) Subprocessors and telemetry
- Core subprocessors (cloud infra, monitoring) are required; we'll provide a list and offer a path to restrict some analytics if needed.
- EU-US transfers: for data residency in EU we can serve inference in eu-west and keep logs in-region; transfer of logs out of region would require customer consent or dedicated deployment.

4) Operational impact and timeline
- Spinning a Dedicated pool with regional residency usually takes 3–4 weeks (provisioning, network peering, KMS/HSM integration).
- Short-term option: Hosted + configuration to drop request payloads and a strict ingestion filter for PHI for initial pilot (2–3 days to configure).

Attachment: runtime-residency-notes.txt (summary of technical constraints and options)

I'll join the call today and can sketch out cost/lead-time tradeoffs.

— Markus
Director, Product Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: HarborBank privacy addendum feasibility — legal perspective

Notes from legal after quick review:

- Contract approach: for clarity we typically provide a primary DPA with addenda for vertical-specific obligations. For this case I recommend a single consolidated "Regulated Addendum" attached to the DPA that enumerates GLBA obligations and includes a BAA section for PHI. That keeps a single signatory flow for the pilot.
- Subprocessor list: we will provide a signed list of subprocessors and a 30-day notice period for material additions. Harbor is likely to request a right to audit or SOC2 evidence — we should prepare our SOC2 + ISO artifacts and an exec summary.
- Logging/PHI: we can agree to no persistent PHI logging for covered routes; legal will propose restrictive language and an option to have longer retention only under explicit, documented consent. We should be careful with "guarantee" language — phrase as contractual commitment with defined exceptions (e.g., compelled by law).
- EU-US transfer: if Harbor requires EU residency for model weights and logs, Dedicated or Private will be required. For Hosted, we can offer in-region inference but not exclusive physical isolation.

Action items for the pilot:
1) Draft consolidated Regulated Addendum (I started a draft: Draft_Addendum_v0.3.docx).
2) Produce a short evidence package: SOC2 summary, encryption architecture, KMS/HSM options.
3) Confirm provisioning timeline (Markus) and provide a pricing delta for Dedicated vs. Hosted configuration.

I'll attach the draft addendum and push a redline after we hear Harbor's preference.

— Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Draft_Addendum_v0.3.docx
